To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a 3-D analytical model for the magnetic interaction in remotely controlled magnetic devices.

we have developed an analytical model and experimental results for a magnetic field created by a multiple ASM system and a magnetic torque transmitted to a magnetic capsule that has arbitrary positions and orientations.
the torque imparted onto a permanent magnet can be controlled by the external rotating magnetic field and can be used to actuate a drug release mechanism in a capsule robot.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the analysis and control of remotely controlled magnetic devices and the application of this technology to the design of a capsule robot that can perform targeted drug delivery in the human gastrointestinal tract.
the development of a magnetic system to remotely control a capsule robot that has been designed to deliver drugs to a specific location in the body.
the analysis of the torque generated by a rotating magnetic field and its application to the actuation of a magnetic device.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed a new analytical method to predict the torque imparted on a small permanent magnet in a magnetic device that has an arbitrary orientation and position with respect to the rotating field.

the analytical model developed in this paper can be used as an effective and accurate design tool for remotely controlled magnetic devices, such as capsule robots, and that this model is also useful in the development of real-time control strategies.
the analysis of magnetic interactions in remotely controlled magnetic devices is essential for establishing real-time control strategies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established a methodology for designing and controlling magnetic interaction for a variety of applications in remotely controlled magnetic devices.
the analytical and experimental results show a good correlation, and the results of this study can be used to design and develop magnetic capsule robots for drug delivery.
we have successfully developed a magnetic actuation method for a capsule robot that can be actuated in any position and at any inclination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic torque transmitted to the capsule robot is a function of the orientation of the robot and the distance between the capsule robot and the magnetic field source.

the torque imparted by the magnetic field created from multiple ASMs is not only a function of the position and orientation of the capsule robot, but also a function of the relative position and orientation between the capsule robot and the ASMs.
we have demonstrated a method of actuating the drug release mechanism of a capsule robot without requiring the capsule to be in a specific position or orientation.
